workflow_rationale: This is a new capability being added to the existing task management system. It introduces a novel user-facing feature that enhances the task creation experience without modifying core existing functionality. The feature builds on top of existing infrastructure (Claude SDK, Electron IPC) while adding net-new UI and backend handlers.

phases.name: Backend AI Refinement Service
phases.description: Create the AI refinement service using Claude Haiku and wire it to IPC handler

subtasks.description: Create task_refinement.py service with Claude Haiku integration

verification.command: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'apps/backend'); from ideation.task_refinement import refine_task_with_ai; print('OK')"

subtasks.notes: Created task_refinement.py service with Claude Haiku integration. Implements refine_task_with_ai() function that expands brief task descriptions into structured task data with title, description, category, priority, complexity, and impact fields. Follows async context manager pattern from claude_client.py and SDK availability pattern from insight_extractor.py.

subtasks.description: Add IPC handler for task refinement in task-handlers.ts

verification.instructions: Check that IPC_CHANNELS.TASK_REFINE handler is registered in task-handlers.ts and calls the Python task_refinement service

subtasks.notes: Created refinement-handlers.ts with IPC handler for 'task:refine' channel. The handler spawns a Python process to call task_refinement.refine_task_with_ai from ideation/task_refinement.py. Returns TaskRefinementResult with title, description, category, priority, complexity, and impact fields. Includes 60s timeout, proper error handling, and IPCResult format. Registered in task/index.ts. Documentation updated in task-handlers.ts.
Added TASK_REFINE: 'task:refine' to IPC_CHANNELS in apps/frontend/src/shared/constants/ipc.ts. Verified constant is properly exported through the re-export chain.

phases.name: Frontend IPC API Layer
phases.description: Add task refinement API method to the frontend preload API

subtasks.description: Add refineTask method to TaskAPI interface and implementation
subtasks.notes: Added refineTask method to TaskAPI interface and implementation. Added TaskRefinementResult type to shared/types/task.ts with fields: title, description, category, priority, complexity, impact. Implementation uses ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC_CHANNELS.TASK_REFINE, briefDescription) to communicate with the backend handler.

phases.name: Frontend UI Integration
phases.description: Add 'Refine with AI' button to TaskCreationWizard and implement form population logic

subtasks.description: Add isRefining state and handleRefineWithAI function

verification.instructions: Verify that TaskCreationWizard.tsx contains isRefining state and handleRefineWithAI async function that calls window.electronAPI.refineTask

subtasks.notes: Added isRefining state and handleRefineWithAI async function to TaskCreationWizard.tsx. The function calls window.electronAPI.refineTask(description) and populates all form fields on success. Also updated handleClose to prevent closing during refinement.

subtasks.description: Add 'Refine with AI' button to the form UI

verification.instructions: Open task creation wizard and verify 'Refine with AI' button appears near the description field

subtasks.notes: Added 'Refine with AI' button to TaskCreationWizard.tsx. Imported Sparkles icon from lucide-react. Button positioned below description field inline with helper text. Uses ghost variant with Sparkles icon (or Loader2 when refining). Disabled when isCreating, isRefining, or description is empty. Shows 'Refining...' loading state during AI refinement.

subtasks.description: Add toast notifications for success and error states

verification.instructions: Test refinement and verify toast appears on success and error cases

subtasks.notes: Added toast notifications for AI refinement success and error states. Created reusable toast component system using @radix-ui/react-toast with success and destructive variants. Integrated Toaster in App.tsx and added toast calls in TaskCreationWizard.tsx handleRefineWithAI function.

phases.name: End-to-End Integration Testing
phases.description: Verify the complete flow from button click to form population works correctly

subtasks.description: End-to-end verification of task refinement flow

steps: Verify all fields auto-populate: title, description, category, priority, complexity, impact
Verify user can edit any populated field
Verify toast notification appears on success

subtasks.notes: E2E verification completed successfully. Fixed TypeScript type definition for ElectronAPI to include refineTask method. Added browser mock for testing. All integration points verified: IPC channel defined, preload API connected, main process handler registered, UI button functional with loading states and toast notifications. Build passes. Feature ready for QA acceptance testing.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: Sequential execution required due to dependencies (backend → API layer → UI)
parallelism.reasoning: Phase 1 must complete before Phase 2 (IPC handler must exist before API can call it). Phase 2 must complete before Phase 3 (API must be available before UI can use it). Phase 4 is integration testing that depends on all previous phases.

summary.startup_command: This is an Electron desktop app. To test: npm run dev (in apps/frontend). Backend runs automatically as Electron main process.

acceptance_criteria: New code has test coverage for task_refinement.py
Button appears in task creation form
Form fields populate with AI-generated content
Error handling works for API failures

verification_steps.expected_outcome: Button works, fields populate, errors handled gracefully

verification_steps.name: Browser Verification
verification_steps.command: npm run dev and verify UI in running app
verification_steps.expected_outcome: Button appears, loading states work, toast notifications show

verification_strategy.reasoning: Medium risk requires unit and integration tests. This is a user-facing feature with AI integration, so proper error handling and UX polish are critical. Backend needs unit tests for prompt construction and response parsing. Frontend needs tests for form state management and IPC communication.
